plain: Sharp and clever in judging people or deals

webster.text: Having the qualities of a shrew; vexatious; troublesome; mischievous.

more.text: Sly; cunning; arch; subtil; artful; astute; as a shrewd man.
Sagacious; of nice discernment; as a shrewd observer of men.

example.quote: Advert to the contemptuous manner in \vhich a shrewd politician speaks of our government.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 3, Virginia Convention, June 6, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
